1.א: Who cooks food or spices, or heats water [even water drinkable without cooking, likewise milk — liable because it improves through cooking], or bakes bread — all one category [baking is bishul for bread; “bishul” for other foods]. Melting any metal or heating metal until charcoal — toladata of bishul [softening for repair]. Likewise melting wax/tallow/milk/pitch/tar/sulfur — toladata, liable. Firing clay until pottery — bishul [the clay “cooks” before kiln]. Putting wood in the oven to dry when moisture leaves — liable for bishul. Generally hardening the soft or softening the hard — liable [Rambam ch. 9]: beware placing wet wood on the oven after sunset (Torah concern). Meat on coals: a complete roast of kezayit — liable even from several spots; if only “ma’achal ben deruso” — still liable, but then the meat must be roasted on both sides [else exempt, Rambam]. All this for chatat; Torah prohibition applies more broadly; Rambam’s kezayit measure for roasting is for chatat; half a shiur is forbidden from the Torah [Shabbat 74a, Rashi].
1.ב: On Shabbat: whenever there is doubt whether something counts as bishul (or similarly other melachot of this kind), do not forbid it bedieved, because this prohibition is only rabbinic (a penalty), and safek derabanan le-kula [Pri Megadim — alef yud; similarly Magen Avraham siman 323 sk 11; see sk 32 and Taz sk 101].
1.ג: One of the other melachot: if it is only derabanan, see Biur HaGRA, who elaborates to prove that all agree that if done be-shogeg one does not forbid benefiting from it bedieved; see Baer Hetev.
1.ד: Always: one may not benefit from that melacha they fined; still, one may benefit from its monetary value. Magen Avraham cites Rashba: the pot in which he cooked on Shabbat is also forbidden for him to cook in afterward because it absorbed from what is forbidden to him — specifically one who cooked for a healthy person; one who cooked for a sick person, the pot is permitted.
1.ה: Permitted at motza’ei Shabbat immediately — even for what was cooked for him — we require kedei sheyaasu only for work done by a gentile for a Jew (because amira le’akum is treated strictly). Something done by a Jew himself need not wait — no concern he will next ask a Jew to cook on Shabbat for this; besides, a Jew will not listen — “ein adam choteh velo lo.” If motza’ei was Yom Tov, even if he cooked permissibly (e.g., for a sick person on Shabbat), a healthy person is still forbidden on the first day of YT — Shabbat does not prepare YT. If on Shabbat something deliberately cooked became mixed with others: Magen Avraham holds it is not batel and he may not benefit on Shabbat — since at motza’ei it will be permitted for others it is “davar she-yesh lo matirin.” What is written in YD end of siman 102 the opposite — Magen Avraham strained to resolve; see Chotem Daat who argues. This [stringency] is for the cook himself; for others all agree “yesh lo matirin.”
1.ו: And be-shogeg: mistaken in halakhah or forgot — all is called shogeg.
1.ז: Also for others: the Gemara disputes shogeg vs. mezid (R. Meir vs. R. Yehuda). Shulchan Aruch follows R. Yehuda, as Rif, Rambam, and Geonim [Gra in his commentary agrees with Tosafot’s allies who hold like R. Meir:] for mezid forbidden to him and others until motza’ei; for shogeg permitted even to himself immediately. In pressing need one may rely on this for [eating] bishul done be-shogeg.

2.ח: Fell ill today: we do not say the animal is muktzeh because of shechita — it was not intended for shechita earlier when there was no illness; we hold like R. Shimon who has no muktzeh unless “pushed aside by hand” (e.g. a lamp lit for that Shabbat); an animal was not “pushed aside”; see Beit Yosef.
2.ט: The healthy person may [eat raw at night] — because the shechita is essentially for the sick person (no kezayit without shechita), and “lest they increase for him” does not apply the same way.
2.י: Raw on Shabbat; without salting — salting is forbidden, and rinsing [raises] visible blood; absorbed blood that did not separate has no issur in this way.
2.יא: Forbidden to the sick [to eat the cooked food on Shabbat — text nuance]; at motza’ei permitted immediately without kedei. “Taste”: if the stew is good for the sick person it is permitted even on Shabbat [for the sick].
2.יב: Where there is no danger: he is like a healthy person for this — Torah forbids cooking for him by a Jew; we fear if we permit eating they will increase cooking for him.
2.יג: “Lest they increase for him”: putting meat into the pot — Torah prohibition when they add for him, even if they add once before putting the pot on the fire; some say derabanan because it is one action [see Beit Yosef; Magen Avraham; Ahavat Chesed ch. 7 proves primary view is first opinion].
2.יד: Forbidden on Shabbat for a healthy person to benefit; motza’ei immediately permitted — because the gentile cooked permissibly, no kedei; no decree of bishulei akum [Gra].
2.טו: Erev: even if from erev he intended to cut the fruit on Shabbat — forbidden, because hachanah does not help for attached [fruit] that is still growing on Shabbat; if growth finished, hachanah helps even attached; an ill person who fell ill today — in all cases forbidden to the healthy because of muktzeh of attached [produce].
2.טז: That still grows: Magen Avraham asks — let the growing parts be batel in the majority heter; Gra leans that way le-halakhah.

3.יז: In a derivative of fire: one is liable; therefore placing fruit or water on the oven or in the cookstove after the oven was heated and [food] cooked there — liable; derabanan forbidden even before heating [below]. All bishul rules in this siman apply also to what was cooked by fire’s derivative.
3.יח: Even in sun-heat: even bedieved forbidden; perhaps after Shabbat even for the cook himself permitted [Gra chiddushim].
3.יט: To insulate… even [substances] from weekday are forbidden if they add heat (explained siman 257 sk 3); forbidden to insulate even from erev [Rosh]. Gra cites Rashba: permitted from erev if heated from sun before Shabbat — it fully cools Friday night.
3.כ: In hot sand: even only rolling on hot sand to roast — forbidden; decree against fire-derivatives; therefore forbidden to roast an egg on a sun-heated roof. “Cooking” in Teveria hot springs — exempt from chatat (sun-derivative) but malkot derabanan; therefore forbidden to place food on them on Shabbat; may leave from erev; placing inside [the spring] forbidden because of hatmana in a heat-increasing medium (siman 326 sk 3).
3.כא: But in the sun itself — we do not decree sun vs. fire (they are not confused).

4.כב: “If it has…” every prohibition because of bishul — even putting on the kirah toward the oven before stoking is forbidden, siman 253.
4.כג: Bishul: Torah forbidden to leave this dish on Shabbat in a hot place with yad soledet; mixing it into boiling [food] in kli sheini — acharonim are lenient.
4.כד: If “cooled” means no yad soledet — even if slightly warm; if yad soledet remains, even if “cooled” from boiling, no further bishul — it is still “boiling” and there is no bishul achar bishul [specifically returning to the oven when garuf…; to un-garuf oven or fire — forbidden for all even fully boiling, siman 253]. This is the Mechaber; Rema below sk 16 Hagah: while not fully cooled, custom is lenient — see there.
4.כה: “Good for it” (mitztamek ve-yafeh lo): but if mitztamek ve-ra lo — permitted to place near a bonfire even where yad soledet; Bach [follows] first side; Gra seems so.
4.כו: Ma’achal ben deruso: even more until fully cooked — Torah bishul.
4.כז: Even while still boiling: obviously a gentile may not finish; bedieved there is room to rely on poskim that once ma’achal ben deruso there is no [further] bishul.
4.כח: “These words…” when cooled there is bishul in all variations.
4.כט: Soup: because liquid cooled, the first “name” of bishul is gone.
4.לא: Already cooked: specifically cooked; if it was only soaked erev in kli rishon with yad soledet — forbidden to soak Shabbat in yad soledet — slight increase in cooking; some lenient; Pri Megadim explains leniency for things that finish easily in kli rishon off fire; if not their nature — all forbid; good to be strict. Regarding soaking in kli sheini yad soledet — lenient if erev it was soaked in yad soledet.
4.לב: And it is dry: the gravy was poured off.
4.לג: Permitted to soak: even in boiling kli rishon so it softens and becomes liquid — no bishul achar bishul; do not put in kli rishon on the fire.
4.לד: That [soaking] in hot water yad soledet: even if one does not leave until fully soft; kli sheini also forbidden to soak — looks like bishul; unlike spices in sk 9 [which only improve taste].
4.לה: “We rinse”: pouring from kli sheini; from kli rishon forbidden — iruy cooks kedei kelipa; likewise pouring kli sheini onto cold liquid is mere rinsing [acharonim].
4.לו: Except “old salted” fish: kulyas etc. — their rinsing completes the melacha / bishul; Gemara chatat; acharonim: if only edible through hot rinse it is bishul; if cold rinse suffices — lenient; local “herring” — practice to be strict per Sheiset / customs.
4.לז: Their rinsing in cold: permitted; even soaking until edible — anything not edible may be made edible on Shabbat (siman 324).
4.לח: So any hard item: edible raw but too hard — soaking to eat is rabbinically “completing” like old salt [Rema].
4.לט: Forbidden to soak — even kli sheini; likewise anything made edible by mere hot rinse — rinsing also forbidden; same for salted fish. Tea leaves on Shabbat: poskim agree there is bishul; mezid skila, shogeg chatat — be very careful; many stumble on weak heterim. Pouring kli rishon onto tea leaves is certainly a Torah concern — we hold iruy is “cooking kedei kelipa”; standing on the stove until yad soledet is worse. Even pouring water first then putting leaves to make “kli sheini” is often forbidden — food not in hot water before Shabbat may not be soaked even kli sheini; soft leaves may cook from rinse — Torah concern. Acharonim: erev Shabbat pour boiling kli rishon on leaves so tea is “partially cooked” by iruy; stir well so leaves cook kedei kelipa; pour off liquid so leaves are dry — then on Shabbat pouring kli rishon is like dry cooked food (no bishul achar bishul even if cooled). Cold essence may be returned to cup [liquid cooled — rules of liquid]. Coffee: same care; do not pour kli rishon unless soaked erev as above. Even after heter: do not leave tea/coffee on stove — erev only partial cook by iruy; full cooking on stove would complete bishul. Best: prepare essence completely erev so no further hot pour needed; morning put cold essence in cup and add hot from kli sheini; cold milk permitted; no kli rishon pour without the erev preparation [see Chatam Sofer responsa; Perishah].

5.מ: If they then cooked it in liquid — meaning placed in the pot while cooking with gravy; if put in cold liquids, already there is bishul for the liquids.
5.מא: Because of bishul: even though there is no bishul achar bishul for dry, there is bishul achar tzliyah/afiyah even still hot from roasting [acharonim]; likewise tzliyah achar bishul — therefore forbidden to put something cooked without gravy near fire [Magen Avraham]; not only at fire — anywhere roasting could occur from oven heat; beware returning baked meat without gravy into oven in yad soledet spot; even on intervening pot; but all agree no tzliyah achar tzliyah — roasted may go to fire even cooled, provided not too close lest stir coals; not on oven floor without intervening empty vessel [siman 253 sk 5]; same for baking.
5.מב: Forbidden to put bread… another rule: some hold soft things cook even kli sheini — we are not expert; therefore added bread (soft) even kli sheini; likewise other items — strict kli sheini; see below sk 9 spices.
5.מג: They permit kli sheini — hold kli sheini never cooks anything.
5.מד: Even kli rishon — hold no bishul achar afiyah/tzliyah; vice versa.
5.מה: People are careful: not to put bread in “tsholent” gravy in kli sheini bowl; all the more not to pour kli rishon; those who cut onions into soup in bowl — wait until soup not yad soledet; bread is lenient because baked; onions need care — we don’t know “soft”; all the more onions into thick stew — some hold solid gush in kli sheini is like kli rishon. Even if soup cooled — beware pouring more soup from pot if yad soledet — iruy Torah concern sk 10. “Hooves soup” — cutting bread and pouring kli rishon gravy not good; even pouring first to make kli sheini — Rema says beware; wait until not yad soledet or ladle so bowl is kli shlishi; onions/shallots into hot liquid — extreme care.
5.מו: Lechatchila… bedieved even kli rishon do not forbid — rely on lenient opinions.
5.מז: Even kli sheini — Pri Megadim sk 35 leans lenient kli shlishi.
5.מח: Anything yad soledet: Chayei Adam — where hand is burnt, all agree [effective] cooking even kli sheini.

6.מט: Something hot yad soledet: Mechaber — if cooled somewhat until no yad soledet there is still bishul; per Rema Hagah sk 16 if custom permits until not fully cooled — then we don’t require yad soledet.
6.נ: In it: even not fully cooked — we said there is bishul while “boiling” because here we don’t reach full bishul, only retaining heat [Taz]; many acharonim disagree — only if fully cooked; Maamar Mordekhai: once fully cooked even mitztamek ve-yafeh lo by this standing permitted.
6.נא: To leave covered… insulation in cloths from erev — teaches permitted to put vessel under cloths that covered the pot; hatmana generally forbidden even non-heat — here primary hatmana was erev for the pot — permitted; if pot uncovered, may cover incidentally also vessel with hot food.
6.נב: Mouth in dough: so steam not escape; not muktzeh dough e.g. for chickens. Magen Avraham: only dough not subject to miruah; wax/tar/clay — miruah issur (siman 314 sk 11); Taz says dough also “miruah” but here not miruah… Magen Avraham forbids wax/clay; per Taz permitted in our case.
6.נג: But one may not leave… stew cooled — bishul achar bishul — forbidden even without hatmana; liquid; dry fully cooled — permitted [below sk 8].
6.נד: Upper [vessel] could heat: even if not intending to leave long — fear he will forget [below sk 14].

7.נה: Even bottom vessel… because intervening pot gives recognition — doesn’t look like cooking; when vessel fully cooked.
7.נו: On the fire… intervening pot like garuf kirah — forbidden lechatchila; halakhah like first opinion [above].

8.נז: Placing something cold: this sk and next one same topic — two versions; there liquid if cooled has bishul; here “vessel with hot food”; here dry even cooled no bishul [above].
8.נח: Everything permitted to leave… per sk 4 no bishul — dry even cooled — permitted to soak kli rishon; likewise place opposite bonfire somewhat far — no chitzuy concern [sk 16].
8.נט: Kettle on fire: even garuf kirah only “return” not initial placement [siman 253 sk 5 Hagah]; here kettle intervenes — some hold intervening kettle better than garuf — there pot on kirah looks cooking; here on pot not usual cooking — permitted even lechatchila.
8.ס: First view seems primary: Arukh HaShulchan and Gra; applies to next sk too.
8.סא: Gravy: since gravy, Mechaber held if cooled bishul achar bishul — forbidden on hot kettle even off fire [sk 6].
8.סב: Mitztamek ve-yafeh lo: language from TY; his view mitztamek ve-yafeh lo has bishul achar bishul; halakhah we wrote — poskim don’t split; Mechaber may agree; uses TY wording.

9.סג: As long as… even if boiling stopped.
9.סד: Yad soledet: if no yad soledet even kli rishon doesn’t “cook.” If not removed from fire — forbidden spices even salt; even intent to remove quickly lest forget [below sk 14].
9.סה: Into it spices: kli sheini permitted spices even yad soledet — doesn’t cook there; solid gush yad soledet in kli sheini — beware: some hold like kli rishon.
9.סו: Once removed: on fire even “ox meat” cooks.
9.סז: Ox meat: even if softens kli sheini — not its “cooking” — same cold.
9.סח: Salted meat: salted and rinsed properly.
9.סט: Ox [meat]: meat doesn’t cook but moisture inside cooks [Tur].
9.ע: Without salting… don’t think issur is salt softening — even unsalted forbidden because of moisture; Rema said salted because unsalted would raise blood issur in hot kli without Shabbat issur.
9.עא: Some forbid: Gemara two versions — lenient: salt hard like ox meat — permitted kli rishon off fire; strict: salt cooks kli sheini; most like lenient; machmir blessed. Halakhic salt from mining; salt made by boiling water — no bishul achar bishul for all [sk 16; MA SA]. “Tsuklar” same leniency kli rishon off fire; some doubt; good lechatchila avoid kli rishon.
9.עב: Even if… on fire — forbidden per Shulchan Aruch.
9.עג: Salt batel: though usually flavor-agent not batel — here both contributed; salted erev and new salt not enough for taste alone — if new salt enough for taste forbidden until motza’ei if in pot on fire; mined salt vs boiled salt food — see above.

10.עד: From kli rishon: though spices don’t cook kli sheini, pouring from kli rishon is iruy — cooks kedei kelipa; bedieved forbidden if deliberately poured while stream continuous.

11.עה: Full of hot water: even Teveria water forbidden to put cold into bath fed by spring — take with kli sheini then pour, even little cold into much hot [below sk 12].
11.עו: Even kli sheini: bathing water usually very hot — cold mixed in “cooks” [Tur]; “heats a lot.”
11.עז: Don’t give cold water: acharonim — little cold that could cook there forbidden; much cold until tepid — permitted [like end sk 12]. If bathtub kli rishon — Ran / Yerucham: even much cold may be problem.
11.עח: But he may pour… even kli rishon may pour into much cold water — cold and hot mix and heat nullified; unlike sk 10 solid. Hot meat chunk into cold gravy — forbidden if not mixed — kedei kelipa [Magen Avraham].
11.עט: Into another tub: chumra; all the more other cold vessel.

12.פ: Much cold water: little that could become yas — forbidden; much cold permitted even if could cause “weld” repair of metal vessel — not pesik reisha; if intends repair some say Torah, some derabanan.
12.פא: Into cold or cold into… in both, even little cold after mix if still yas in kli sheini — permitted — kli sheini doesn’t cook [sk 9].
12.פב: Not in kli rishon: if hot in kli rishon forbidden to pour cold in or out into little cold that will cook.
12.פג: If [cold] much: cold into hot or hot into much cold — permitted. Chayei Adam: cold into hot — one big pour; little by little forbidden — immediate cooking.
12.פד: Only to remove cold: even lukewarm ok if not yas.
12.פה: Not on fire: same near fire where could cook — lest forget [sk 14].

13.פו: Pitcher of water: even water without vessel may mix kli sheini [sk 12]; brought via vessel for end — kli rishon even with interrupting vessel forbidden.
13.פז: Kli sheini: all the more if poured from kli rishon into this cup; permitted even yas; if scoop with empty [vessel] from kli rishon some say like kli rishon; if holds empty in pot until hot — kli rishon [acharonim].

14.פח: In a way it cannot… even long time won’t get that hot.
14.פט: Where infant belly… we can’t measure by hand — people differ sensitivity.
14.צ: If it can… fear he will adjust/stir.
14.צא: So fruit: forbidden in heat to remove cold lest cook; even eaten raw if improves — bishul; may place far from fire; even inedible raw — far is ok. May place alunith / earthenware near fire to warm food not yet cooled [davar she-eino mitkaven; will watch before melting].

15.צב: Already cooked: no bishul concern; on actual fire derabanan maris ayin; opposite bonfire people don’t usually cook — no derabanan [Rashba]; Rosh: need small distance; some acharonim: coals inside oven like siman 253 even not on flame; if on intervening vessel lenient [253 sk 3].
15.צג: Fully and dry: if not fully cooked even dry hot still bishul; if liquid even “fully” if cooled can have bishul achar bishul per Mechaber sk 4.
15.צד: Opposite bonfire: need distance from coals so no stir concern [Rosh]. Acharonim: free-standing bonfire vs coals in oven — stricter in oven; on intervening vessel lenient.
15.צה: Even if already cooled: Mechaber’s words — only dry when cooled.
15.צז: Some lenient [positions] argue on the Mechaber: they hold the distinction is only when [food] is dry; but for liquid that cooled there is bishul achar bishul. Another opinion cited here holds there is never bishul achar bishul in any case, even fully cold.
15.צח: On the fire… if one places it actually on the fire — even if there is no Torah prohibition per that view, still rabbinically forbidden because it looks like cooking and lest one stir the coals.
15.צט: On fire… if not… per Mechaber once cooled from heat no yas no bishul; custom lenient if not fully cooled [rely on lenient].

16.ק: “Inpandah” (pasteida): double crust with fat — permitted to warm because dry; even if fat remelts still “dry” if not yet melted when placed [sk 16].
16.קא: Near fire: with intervening vessel; else forbidden [253 sk 3,5].
16.קב: Even if… unlike crushing ice/hail (siman 320 sk 9) nolad — here passive melting; like gemara may put in wine to cool; even if dissolves kidei bamakom.
16.קג: All the more pot… fat mixes into gravy not visible — like “into cup” invisibly melting hail.
16.קד: Permitted: for nolad not a problem; bishul — liquid dish worse: only where no yas [sk 16].
16.קה: Some strict: nolad — fat visible when melted; even in sun. But if not so much fat that it flows out and shows; or far from heat; or removed surface fat — all permit; small oozing from meat — permitted. Hot water / drink crust on top: all permit off yas — dissolves into liquid below invisibly [acharonim].
16.קו: To be strict: before oven stoked may place — some permit after; not in public [Magen Avraham, SA].
16.קז: In need may rely: then even lechatchila; bedieved never forbid.

17.קח: Forbidden to put cold… per Rema Hagah sk 16 if cooked and not fully cooled — lenient.
17.קט: A lot: fear he will forget and leave until cooked.
17.קי: Like rule of leaving… above sk 14: even to remove cold forbidden if could reach bishul.
17.קיא: If not… miḥam on fire see sk 8.
17.קיב: Permitted: even cold never cooked before.

18.קיג: Removed boiling: chumra even off fire if not fully cooked; if fully cooked even on fire ladle out — Beit Yosef; Arukh HaShulchan stricter.
18.קיד: If found stirring… actual stirring worse; chatat if Shulchan Aruch holds it helps cooking [sk 4].
18.קטו: Fully cooked: may stir — no bishul achar bishul [sk 4].
18.קטז: Forbidden to stir: dyeing — constant stir for even absorption [dyeing melacha].
18.קיז: Even in pot… turn pot to plate; don’t ladle; acharonim not strict; bedieved primary: fully cooked may stir; only actual stirring “to be machmir”; ladle from pot not on fire for fully cooked — no need to be strict.

19.קיח: “Opposite the bonfire” — not only: also moving skewer with roast from fire, still yas, forbidden to smear fat on it; even then on plate kli sheini — some poskim hold solid yas gush may “cook” even kli sheini — bedieved rely kli sheini never cooks. Oil / “live” un-cooked fat different from congealed cooked fat — may smear at fire; like sk 16 dry cooked has no bishul; nolad not an issue if absorbed in meat; don’t crush by hand — place bit by bit melting on its own. Same goose fat on grains/legumes on hot bowl yas if added slowly. Tosefta: several supplied fire, wood, pot, water, meat, spices — last stirs, all liable: fire — mab’ir; wood — mab’ir; others bishul; stirrer too. Variants in girsa; Maggid Mishneh; Beit Yosef; Gra on Tosefta. “Not liable if no bishul chatat” — Kitzur; Beit Yosef in Kalbo: on fire stir even fully cooked. Our “samovar” set up erev: do not take water Shabbat if not garuf [Tosafot Yerushalim; fear adding water / repair]. Care if sat to drink before sunset and candle lit mid-meal — do not continue drinking from that pot [per that concern].
